title: Unified Salary Guidelines for Community Care Sector
what_it_is: Unified Salary Guidelines for Community Care Sector

sections.label: Community care salary guidelines
sections.summary: MOH publishes community care salary guidelines, monitors salary movements, funds CCOs, and says CCOs may need to co-fund increases, possibly raising fees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The salary guidelines for the community care sector have been published to provide greater transparency and clarity to jobseekers and community care workers on salaries in the sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: It is in the CCO's own interest to abide by the guidelines, or they will not be competitive in attracting and retaining their staff, or pay them salaries that is commensurate with their contributions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We will continue to monitor the salary movements of community care staff against the recommended salary levels through yearly surveys.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: MOH and the Ministry of Social and Family Development’s (MSF's) salary guidelines apply to the healthcare and social service sectors respectively, as there are differences in the job roles and benchmarked to different sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Nonetheless, MOH and MSF will continue to exchange salary review plans and information on a regular basis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Since 2020, MOH has funded CCOs through the community care salary enhancements exercise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: MOH will continue to fund and support CCOs to adopt the salary guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: However, CCOs will need to co-fund some of the salary increases and these could translate into modest increases in their fees.

sentences.text: Since 2020, MOH has been funding CCOs through the Community Care Salary Enhancements Exercise.
